title: South Korea's Noodle Giants Fight for Global Sales
paragraphs: Two major South Korean food companies, which have long been rivals in their home country, are now fighting for global sales as Korean food becomes more popular overseas.
The companies NongShim and Samyang are both famous for their noodles in South Korea.

Founded in 1961, Samyang became the first South Korean company to sell instant ramen noodles in 1963. But NongShim, founded in 1965, became the country's top instant noodle maker in 1991, and has controlled around 55% of the South Korean market since then.

These days, the two companies' signature brands are quite different. NongShim is famous for its Shin Ramyun: noodles that come with a spicy beef soup and dried vegetables. Samyang, on the other hand, is famous for its Buldak, which means "fire chicken" in Korean. These stir-fried, soupless noodles in chicken sauce are much spicier than Shin Ramyun noodles.

In fact, Buldak noodles have won attention for their extreme spiciness, with videos of people trying the "fire noodle challenge" — eating Buldak noodles as fast as possible — going viral on social media.

Videos like these have helped increase Samyang's global popularity, and international sales now make up 80% of the company's total revenue. Samyang has already overtaken NongShim in markets like China and Europe, and is close behind it in the US.
NongShim's international sales make up just 37% of revenue.

Now NongShim is trying to catch up with Samyang's success abroad by building a factory in Busan that will produce Shin Ramyun noodles for export to Japan, Europe, Australia, India and Southeast Asia. NongShim believes the factory will boost its export capacity by 70%.
By 2030, NongShim wants to double its global noodle sales to 5.4 trillion won, or about $4 billion, which would raise international sales to over 60% of its revenue.
NongShim has also clearly studied Samyang's success with soupless noodles, and it plans to bring out its own stir-fried Shin Ramyun next year.
